science.title: Valorization of cotton waste into cellulose nanocrystals and their incorporation into electrospun poly (vinyl alcohol) nanofibrous membranes with enhanced thermal and structural properties
science.description: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were extracted from cotton waste using alkaline treatment, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis. Increasing the sulfuric acid concentration from 40% to 62% was associated with an increase in CNC yield from approximately 19.20 ± 3.9% to 41.30 ± 3.1%, indicating the influence of acid concentration on the recovery of the nanocrystalline fraction under the conditions employed. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) showed carbon and oxygen as the predominant elements, at 62.39 and 34.33 wt%, respectively, with trace amounts of sulfur and sodium. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed snowflake-like aggregated structures composed of branched rod-like features, with an average width of 56.5 ± 8.7 nm. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed broadly consistent nanoscale morphological features, with snowflake-like structures ranging from approximately 120–200 nm and protruding branches of approximately 63.2 ± 10.9 nm in diameter. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed characteristic cellulose bands, including the band at 872.9 cm⁻¹ associated with β-(1→4)-glycosidic linkages. CNCs were incorporated into poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA) nanofibrous membranes at concentrations of 0–40 wt% via electrospinning. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) of the 40 wt% CNC membrane revealed a relatively uniform fibrous network with a mean fiber diameter of 104.3 ± 38.6 nm, with CNCs distributed on the fiber surfaces. FTIR analysis of the prepared nanofibers showed the characteristic 916 cm⁻¹ band, supporting the presence of the cellulose component. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed an increase in residual mass with increasing CNC content, from 1.28% for the neat PVA membrane to 24.88% for the 40 wt% CNC membrane. Derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) indicated changes in thermal degradation behavior with increasing CNC content. The 40 wt% CNC formulation exhibited the highest residual mass among the studied formulations. The study highlights the successful conversion of cotton waste into CNCs and their incorporation into PVA nanofibrous membranes, with potential applications in advanced packaging and biomedical membranes.

science.title: The chromosome-level genome assembly of the Neotropical yellow-tailed tetra fish Astyanax lacustris (Teleostei: Characiformes)
science.description: Astyanax is one of the most diverse genera of characiform fishes and plays an important role in Neotropical freshwater ecosystems. However, high-quality genomic resources remain scarce for the group, with most available studies focused on the model species Astyanax mexicanus. Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for the yellow-tailed tetra Astyanax lacustris, a widespread and ecologically important species from the upper Paraná River basin, Brazil. The final assembly spans 1.31 Gb, with a scaffold N50 of 49 Mb and 98.8% of the sequence anchored into 25 chromosome-scale scaffolds, corresponding to the expected haploid chromosome number. Assembly completeness was supported by 99.1% complete BUSCOs against the actinopterygii_odb12 dataset. This reference genome provides a valuable foundation for future comparative genomics, evolutionary studies, and conservation genetics of Neotropical fishes.

science.title: Improving deep neural network prediction of hydraulic fracturing initiation pressure in hydrate-bearing sediments through feature engineering and architecture search
science.description: Accurate prediction of hydraulic fracturing initiation pressure ($$P_b$$) in natural gas hydrate-bearing sediments provides screening-level support for laboratory-scale hydraulic fracturing design in NGH-bearing sediments. This study demonstrates that systematic feature engineering and neural architecture search yield substantial improvements for predicting $$P_b$$ on a 114-sample published dataset. The framework first expands the feature space from 12 to 208 variables via polynomial transformations, interaction terms, and domain-specific features, followed by deduplication. Multi-method feature selection identifies a 14-feature subset, and extended evaluation identifies a verified 12$$\times $$32 model as the best-performing saved configuration. The reproducible-by-retraining reference is R$$^2$$ $$\approx $$ 0.87; the verified 12$$\times $$32 saved model achieves R$$^2$$ = 0.92 on its original held-out split and is reported as an upper bound on the dataset. The best of 60 retraining runs reaches 0.85—none reproduces 0.92, confirming that 0.92 is a saved-artifact result, not a reproducible target. The verified 12$$\times $$32 model reduces MSE from 19.34 to 8.22 MPa$$^2$$ and MAE from 3.16 to 2.14 MPa compared to the best prior reported result (R$$^2$$ = 0.81). Feature importance and SHAP analysis show that the model assigns highest importance to stress-composition interactions and stress-derived statistical terms, consistent with known geomechanical controls on fracture initiation. Generalization is modest (CV mean R$$^2 \approx $$ 0.50), and simpler models (RandomForest, SVR) are recommended as production-ready baselines; the 12$$\times $$32 DNN is retained as the best verified saved artifact. These findings confirm that the dataset contains untapped predictive capacity, and that methodological refinement through domain-informed feature engineering combined with systematic architecture search provides an effective pathway for improving prediction fidelity in small-sample geomechanical problems.
